text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended sharply lower as Indonesian and Vietnamese sellers unloaded their stocks. May and July lost $22 to close at $1,698 and $1,758 per tonne, respectively. Distant November and January bucked the trend to finish higher.

The rally earlier this week encouraged Vietnamese producers to unload their stocks, traders in Vietnam said. But there are only 330,000 60-kg bags of coffee left from the current crop after some 4.5 mn bags sold so far, traders said.

Arabica futures in New York ended the week on a quiet note, finishing mostly firmer. July added 1 cent to close at 217.90 cents/lb while September closed 1.05 cents higher at 195.55 cents/lb. On the fundamental side, port workers at Brazil's key port of Santos returned to work on Friday after a one-day strike to protest a delay in receiving the full April salary.
Union officials said the port workers are not considering any further action until they see whether the CODESP port authority fulfills its promise to pay outstanding April salaries on May 13.
The outlook remains very bullish and new highs are likely to be made on a regular basis. FUNDAMENTALS

UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 1,500 bags on May 8 to 26,919 bags from 25,419 bags on May 7 and 24,669 bags on May 6. There were 1,625 bags pending grading in New York, 5,495 bags in New Orleans and 2,000 bags in Miami. Despite the modest rise in certified coffee stocks consumer coffee inventories are still extremely low.

COLOMBIA - According to Merrill Lynch Colombian April coffee production was only 824,000 bags. This is short of the 1 mn bag target the Colombians had earlier anticipated. Sources suggest that targets for the rest of the mitica harvest were also lower, Merrill Lynch said.

May through September production is now estimated at 3.1 mn bags vs 3.5 mn bags previously. This would give a total 1996/97 (October/September) Colombian crop of 9.56 mn bags sharply down from last year's figure of 12.9 mn bags.

BRAZIL - Coffee stocks held by Brazilian cooperatives totalled only 981,475 60.5 kg-bags on April 30, the National Coffee Council (CNC) said. This is down from the 1.49 mn bags held by cooperatives as of March 31 and also below the 1.34 mn bags held at the end of April 1996. The fact stocks are lower at this stage than last year when producers were working with the frost and drought-hit 1995/96 crop shows the higher level of sales by producers, the CNC said. Sales by cooperatives reached 609,063 bags in April vs 731,919 bags during March and 486,371 bags in April last year, showing that producers maintained the flow of coffee to the market, it was added.

SWEDEN - Sweden imported 169,200 bags of coffee in December 1996, 46 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports in calendar year 1996 up to 2.131 mn bags, 29 per cent more than was imported the previous year. Main suppliers of green coffee in 1996 were Kenya (136,700 vs 129,700 bags), Guatemala (190,600 vs 173,200 bags), Brazil (486,700 vs 454,700 bags) and Colombia (467,700 vs 372,200 bags). The country exported 223,000 bags of coffee in 1996, nearly 9 per cent more than was exported the previous year.
